questions.ask: Should a too-long title get its own error message, instead of the generic 'Input is invalid'?
questions.why: The 200-character limit already existed in the domain, the request schemas and the form (the form stops typing at 200). What is missing is the clear message: the repo's shared error contract deliberately turns every validation failure into code invalid_input with the fixed text 'Input is invalid', for all modules. Changing that is a change to an accepted cross-cutting contract, so it is your call.

options.label: Pass safe validation messages through
options.detail: invalid_input errors carry their domain text, e.g. 'Task title must contain 1-200 characters'. Applies to lists too. About an hour, small shared change plus tests.

options.label: Keep the generic message
options.detail: No code change. Browser users never hit it because the form caps input at 200; only direct API callers see 'Input is invalid'. Tonight's tests already lock the limit.

questions.note: Yes, and keep the messages short.

questions.ask: Should 'Clear completed' delete the done tasks for good, or archive them?
questions.why: You asked me not to guess. The two differ in size: delete reuses what exists, archive needs a database change and somewhere to see archived tasks. Note the dashboard already has a 'Show completed tasks' toggle that hides done tasks without deleting anything, which covers much of what archive would give.

options.label: Delete for good
options.detail: One action removes the list's done tasks after a confirm dialog like the existing delete. No database change. About half a day with tests.

options.label: Archive
options.detail: New archived state plus a migration; archived tasks disappear from the list but stay stored. Needs a decision on where people see or restore them. About one to two days.

questions.why: The dashboard sits behind sign-in and needs Postgres. This copy has no .env and no database, and the Docker command that starts the local database needed a permission approval I could not get while you were asleep. The same approval gate also stopped git add and git commit.

options.detail: Open Docker Desktop and approve docker, git add and git commit for this repo. Next session I start the local stack, sign in as a test user, take the screenshot, run the Postgres and e2e suites, and commit. About 20 minutes.

feedback.title: Heredoc JSON input blocked by a common shell safety hook
feedback.body: The skill documents start, record and ask with inline heredoc JSON. A shell safety hook in the agent harness refused that pattern (brace plus quote looks like expansion obfuscation), and redirecting from a temp file outside the repo was refused because the file lay outside the allowed working directory. What worked: writing the JSON into a git-ignored folder inside the repo and redirecting stdin from it. A --file <path> option, plus a documented git-ignored input location (for example under .night-shift/), would remove the guesswork.

feedback.title: Preflight check for unattended permissions before the night starts
feedback.body: Halfway through the night it turned out that git add, git commit and docker all needed an interactive permission approval, so no work could be committed and nothing could run against a database. A start-time preflight (or a documented checklist) that confirms the agent can commit and reach the services the plan needs would surface this while the developer is still awake.
